title: key list
description: What nw-license key list answers with -o json: every key of the signer, its id and its public key, the list apps' builds trust, so the owner copies it into a build without reading a private key (ADR-L6, L7).

apiVersion.description: Always elderlygate/license/app/v1: the form of nw-license's answers. An app's answers keep the family app (apiversion/v1/forms.yaml), apart from the license files they describe.

kind.description: Always KeyList, the kind of this answer, so a reader knows which schema its data meets.

ran.description: Where the answer came from; this contract fixes the app and the contract version, so an answer from anything else fails here.

app.description: Always license, nw-license's product ID, since only nw-license gives this answer (ADR-L7).

contract.description: Always v1, the contract version this schema belongs to.

data.description: Every key of the signer, by id in order; empty when it has none, so a reader tells no key from a failure.

key.description: One signing key as anyone may see it: never its private key, which never leaves the signer (ADR-L6).

id.description: The key's id, which a license's keyId names, so an app finds the public key that checks it (ADR-L6). nw-license makes it a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 long.

publicKey.description: The key's Ed25519 public key, standard base64: 32 bytes, so 44 characters ending =. A build trusts a list of these, so a key can be moved or replaced while the licenses it signed keep working (ADR-L1, L6).

signer.description: The signer backend that keeps the key, so the owner sees where it is; the signer setting picks it. An open word, as backends may be added without changing the rest (ADR-L6). Known words: keychain, the macOS Keychain; file, a key file only the owner can read, on Linux and in a workspace.
